subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session exec overrides continue to outrank later global or agent exec config, or should operator security config and reset semantics override existing session entries?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes a documented session-state and exec-security precedence contract.

options.title: Keep persistence, add reset semantics
options.body: Preserve documented per-session `/exec` defaults but add a clear operator reset, doctor, or migration path for stale exec overrides after security policy changes.

options.title: Make config authoritative
options.body: Change resolution so global or agent exec config wins over stored session fields, accepting the compatibility impact on existing `/exec` session defaults.

options.title: Document current behavior
options.body: Keep stored session overrides as the permanent contract and document that operators must use tool policy, `/new`, or session cleanup to revoke them.

recommendation.title: Keep persistence, add reset semantics
recommendation.body: Preserve documented per-session `/exec` defaults but add a clear operator reset, doctor, or migration path for stale exec overrides after security policy changes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the `/exec` session override implementation, resolver tests, and docs surface.
